title: Session handoff: 0.13.0 board work landed, #486 frozen at 0ae361d3 for the release step
description:
Written at a team boundary before a recycle, 2026-10-03. The deliverable is the implementation note, which carries the state the next session needs; the description exists so the task is findable.

Read the note, not this. Live tracker and live repository outrank both.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The implementation note names the frozen ref, the outstanding blocker and the shape changes a successor must not rediscover
Every claim in the note that a successor would act on is one this session measured, and says so
Nothing in the note asks the successor to act on a cursor or a memory rather than on the tracker

implementationNotes:
HANDOFF, 2026-10-03, written at a team boundary before a recycle. `origin/dev` is `bc0659bf554904d731b03886517db783be79ddee`; nothing is In Progress on it, verified by listing rather than assumed.

**#486 IS FROZEN AT `0ae361d32cec8e3ca689070bb4b0becc1c4a3cf7`.** Do not add a commit to `chore/QCLI-433-bump-0-13-0`. That head is the final 0.13.0 tree for lore-cli's `QUEST_SOURCE_REF`, and the orchestrator asked for it frozen twice.

WHAT IS DONE THERE. QCLI-433's AC2 is executed and verified: all six platform packages rebuilt at 0.13.0 with bun 1.4.2 -- fetched from the release and checksum-verified against the release's own SHASUMS256.txt, NOT the machine's 1.3.14 -- with `check:packages` and `check:lockfile` both exit 0, and the native darwin-arm64 binary runs and reports 0.13.0. AC2's checkbox is DELIBERATELY left unchecked: checking it is a tracker write, a tracker write is a commit, and a commit moves the frozen head. Set it at the release step.

**THE BINARY PROVENANCE CAVEAT IS AN OPEN OPERATOR DECISION, not a defect to fix.** CI builds each target on its OWN NATIVE RUNNER (QUEST_BUN_TARGET per matrix row: ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-14, macos-15-intel, windows-2022, windows-11-arm), and the workflow states that Bun's `--compile` output is not byte-reproducible, which is why a tag runs `--verify-committed` instead of rebuilding. Only darwin-arm64 was built natively here; the other five were cross-compiled by the same bun version. They match their own regenerated manifests, but no native runner has executed them. The orchestrator put this to the operator as a choice: smoke-test on the linux and win VMs before the tag, or rely on tag-time verification. If the answer is smoke-test, the orchestrator will send steps.

WHY #486 READS RED, so a successor does not chase it: its `lore check` failure is the PAIR-RULE red -- lore 0.12.0 requires quest 0.12.0 -- and it clears only when lore 0.13.0 is on npm. `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED is that, not a broken branch.

**THE BOARD'S ENTRY POINT CHANGED SHAPE, TWICE, and this is the thing most likely to be rediscovered the hard way.** There is NO board slash command at all -- `quest-board` and the attempted `quest` are both gone. The board is reached through `mcp__opum-quest__dashboard`, registered at session.start and served from a tool.call hook, and the GENERATED `quest` skill routes to it. The rename to `quest` was tried first and the engine REFUSED the registration because the plugin's own skill owns that name -- and the refusal threw the whole session.start hook, so the board never initialised. `claude plugin validate --strict` and a green 21-test mod suite both passed on that broken tree; only a live session showed it. That is why QCLI-443 (a `claude -p --plugin-dir` live-session probe for release prep) exists and is unstarted.

**SEQ 182 AMENDED CODE THAT HAD ALREADY MERGED** (QCLI-444, PR #501): the batched toast no longer names a retired command, both decision toasts name their repository, the tool result reads `$.ui.panes()` and only claims success when the pane is BOTH placed and shown, and a `Quest board ready` band with an Open button (`o`) gives a narrow terminal a way in. The band-button measurement is positive: at 100 columns an unasked open returns isPlaced false, and a button press seats the pane. Anything built against the pre-#501 board needs re-reading.

NEXT WORK, filed and not started: 0.14.0 is QCLI-445 (question record and commands), QCLI-446 (pane answer interface plus the forgery guard, with a positive control), QCLI-447 (wider decision record), QCLI-448 (task blockers naming a question id -- MEASURE what the blockers field supports first, since QCLI-251 records it has no write path at all), QCLI-449 (prompt capture behind captureRequests). QCLI-437 stays in 0.14.0, decided A.

ONE PROCESS FIX, and it is prevention rather than detection. Three tasks this session were left In Progress after their PRs merged (QCLI-442, QCLI-439, QCLI-444) -- all three carried by a SPECIALIST, and the cause was this session's dispatch briefs: each asked the specialist to check its acceptance criteria against evidence and never asked it to complete the task. Put this line in every brief: check the criteria, then run `quest task complete <id>` ON THE BRANCH and commit the move with the work, so it rides the PR. The fleet sweep already DETECTS this shape ("In Progress, all acceptance criteria checked"); what was missing was prevention. The third instance happened after the lesson had been written down, so treat it as a brief-template defect, not a memory gap.

SKILLS WORTH REACHING FOR: opum-handoff (restore), opum-sdlc (branch/PR/land/promote and the no-exemption rule), opum-quest:quest, opum-lore:lore.

HANDOFF, SECOND WRITE, 2026-10-03 -- written AFTER the orchestrator's recycle request, which is what makes this one count. The note above carries the full state and is NOT superseded; this one records the state at the recycle boundary, what changed since, and one correction that only a live branch switch could expose.

STATE AT THIS BOUNDARY, each verified rather than remembered:
- `origin/dev` is `2e0301f0bfc858ebf3fa6a2855a8f3f2132be807`, local dev fast-forwarded level with it, working tree clean.
- **#486 is UNTOUCHED at `0ae361d32cec8e3ca689070bb4b0becc1c4a3cf7`** (`git rev-parse origin/chore/QCLI-433-bump-0-13-0`), never pushed to, and it must stay that way -- it is lore-cli's `QUEST_SOURCE_REF`.
- **Zero tasks In Progress on dev** (`quest task list --status "In Progress" --json` -> length 0).
- QCLI-444's closure landed in #503, and this handoff record itself landed in #504. Both merged.

**A LIVE INSTANCE OF THE BRANCH-SCOPED TRAP, caught while writing this and worth more than the description of it.** I had finished the session on `chore/QCLI-433-bump-0-13-0`, and running the In Progress listing THERE reported **QCLI-444, In Progress** -- a task that had already been closed on dev eleven commits earlier. Nothing was wrong with the tracker; the listing reads the checked-out branch's `.quest/`. Read on dev it is empty. So: **run the listing on dev, never on whatever branch you happen to be sitting on**, and if a closed task reappears as In Progress, suspect the branch before the record.

ONE ITEM I CAUGHT ONLY BECAUSE OF THAT SWITCH: the session had been left checked out on the FROZEN branch. The recycle instruction is to finish on dev, and a commit made from that checkout would have moved the head the orchestrator asked twice to freeze. That is the concrete risk the "finish on dev" rule protects against, not a formality.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, unchanged from the note above and both still live:
1. **The binary provenance question is with the operator.** Five of six platform packages were cross-compiled on this machine rather than built on CI's native runners, so they have been verified by hash against their own regenerated manifests but NEVER EXECUTED. The choice offered was a native smoke test on the linux and win VMs before the tag, or relying on the tag-time `--verify-committed` on each runner.
2. **QCLI-443, the `claude -p --plugin-dir` live-session probe, is filed and unstarted.** It is the gate that would have caught the `session.start` registration refusal, so 0.13.0 ships without it and 0.14.0 should not.

NEXT ACTION, one: nothing in this repository until the operator answers the binary question. The release is the orchestrator's to drive; the lore-check pair-rule red on #486 clears only when lore 0.13.0 reaches npm, and the paired publish is the operator's.
